analysis:
The PR changes documentation only: docs/provider/cli-reference.md (line 2183, the `enabled_models` row) and docs/provider/troubleshooting.md (the date at line 3 and new rows at lines 170-172). No executable code, configuration defaults, keys, or trust-boundary implementations change. The remaining cli-reference lines supplied (2135-2479) are unchanged context. I examined them against the Paths and identifiers table, the environment passthrough and the prefix-cache/SSD content (T-041) and found no new drift.

The new documentation says `enabled_models`, when set, also bounds coordinator model commands and rollouts. It also says a coordinator command or rollout never adds a model outside the filter. Provider 0.10.6 or earlier follows rollouts regardless of the filter and re-downloads a deselected or removed build. This describes provider-side filtering of coordinator-initiated model changes, which touches TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider WebSocket) and A-004 (model weights, T-012/T-027). It is a documentation claim only. Its accuracy depends on the unseen provider implementation (the reference `configuration.md#provider-model-selection` anchor and the desired_models convergence code), so I could not verify it. The troubleshooting text that older providers are affected is consistent with a hardening, not a regression.

The `desired_models ... not converging` row says the coordinator routes the public model to the newer build first. This is routing behavior owned by the platform and outside this repo's scope. The troubleshooting text advises `darkbloom switch`, with no privileged or insecure action and no secrets. No change to attestation, App Attest, keys, cache storage or fan-helper behavior.

Open question for integration: confirm that the code implementing the enabled_models filter for coordinator commands exists and matches these claims. It is not in the supplied evidence, so documentation accuracy is unverified. This is not a security finding.
